text:
maria: Hey team — ACME POC asks for a 3-month dedicated commit. They want 8 GPUs (mix of A100/H100), autoscale + burst buffer, and want to know if we can net burst across regions. Need pricing + approval path by EOD.
ben: Quick read — two parts: (1) base commit pricing (monthly GPU reserved) and (2) burst/overage rates for autoscale. For an 8-GPU commit here's a rough math example.
ben: Base assumptions: A100 = $6,000/gpu-month, H100 = $9,600/gpu-month (list internal ratecard). Burst = $2.00/gpu-hour for A100, $3.00/gpu-hour for H100. We can offer a stack discount for multi-month commits.
ben: Example (6xA100 + 2xH100): base = 6*6,000 + 2*9,600 = $36,000 + $19,200 = $55,200/mo. For 3 months = $165,600. If we apply a 10% commit discount -> $148, (wait) -> $148, (fix) $148,? (see calc below)
ben: Clean calc: monthly = $55,200 -> 3mo = $165,600. 10% off -> $149,040 total over 3 months (or $49,680/mo).
ben: Burst cost estimate: if they use an additional 4 GPU-hours/day of burst (mixed) -> ~120 GPU-hours/mo -> ~ $240/mo for A100 portion per GPU type. Burst costs are small relative to commit but important for SLOs.
ben: For mixed pools we bill a weighted unit: treat A100 as 1.0, H100 as 1.6 for commit sizing and pricing. That makes it easier to convert to a single SKU-equivalent.
ben: Ops note: autoscale grace_period (e.g., 300s) helps avoid brief spin-ups charging burst every minute. Recommend setting grace_seconds=300 and burst_buffer=50% of pool.
sasha: Ops/infra input — important: Dedicated pools cannot be "shared" across regions. You cannot net burst across geographically separate Dedicated clusters. We can do mirrored pools with failover, but burst capacity is local to each pool. If ACME needs cross-region failover, deploy separate dedicated pools in each region and use smart routing.
sasha: Also: mixed-GPU pools are supported but reduce packing efficiency; if they care about latency for short sequences prefer homogeneous pools.
ben: Here's a sample commit config they can review:

```yaml
dedicated_commit:
  name: acme-poc-commit
  duration_months: 3
  gpus:
    - type: a100
      count: 6
    - type: h100
      count: 2
  autoscale:
    min: 2
    max: 12
    burst_buffer: 4
    grace_seconds: 300
```

ben: With that config, billing will reserve the 8 GPUs (by weighted units) and autoscale will permit up to 12 active nodes using burst; burst-hours billed at overage rate above reserved baseline.
elaine: Deal desk / finance view — if total commit value (post-discount) > $200k we need VP of Revenue sign-off and legal must approve special terms. For a 3-month $149k value it's fine via standard deal desk, but if they push for deeper discounts or extended termination clauses escalate.
elaine: Also need to confirm revenue recognition (monthly vs upfront) and whether they want a PO. If they want a netting clause (use credits across regions) legal will ask for engineering confirmation — likely a non-starter.
tim: Pricing flexibility — we can offer up to 12% discount if they commit to 6 months or increase size by 25%. For 3 months the commercial floor is 8–10% depending on LGTM from CRO.
deal-bot: Ratecard link (internal): https://internal.redwood.com/ratecard/dedicated — attach case id RED-4201 for approvals.
sasha: Technical follow-up: backup plan if autoscale bursts fail — we can route to hosted endpoints as fallback but note differences in latency and data isolation. Also recommend prefix/KV cache warmup to avoid cold-cache latency on scale-ups.
maria: Customer asked if we can offer a short pilot (2 weeks) before signing commit; we can do a time-limited demo pool (non-billed trial) but it won't count toward commit months unless they convert within 7 days. Ops needs a ticket to provision.
maria: Action items: Ben to finalize a written quote (include weighted-SKU math & burst rates), Elaine to start the approval ticket (RED-4201) and route to legal if customer asks for netting clause, Sasha to confirm regional pool constraints with provisioning ETA. Will update ACME this afternoon.
ben: I'll drop a formal quote by 14:00 PST and include the optional 10%/6mo path. :thumbsup:
elaine: Received — I'll create the deal desk card and tag legal if they push netting/termination language.
maria: Thanks all, filing request now.
